title: Graph visualization in a legacy application
summary: Render, edit and interact with graph data in the existing legacy application. Assess whether to keep the deprecated AntV X6 v2 stack as a tactical bridge, migrate to the maintained v3 core, or replace the suite. v2 uses separate 2.x plugins; v3 bundles the official plugins and has different runtime and packaging requirements. Preserve existing graph behaviour during any upgrade or migration.
constraints: Must run within the legacy application's existing browser and runtime baseline; record the exact baseline before judging compatibility
Preserve existing graph editing, selection, transform, history and export behaviour during any upgrade or migration
Permissive license across the full dependency tree
No unfixed high or critical advisories
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Do not mix X6 major lines: v3 core must use its bundled plugins, and 2.x plugins must not be installed with v3
If the application runtime includes Node or SSR, verify native ESM/CJS loading before adopting X6 v3
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap
out_of_scope: Backend graph database and query language
Rewriting the legacy application or choosing a new UI framework
Detailed benchmark against every graph library
notes: The requirement covers two distinct X6 lines. v2: @antv/x6@2.19.2 plus @antv/x6-common, @antv/x6-geometry and the separate 2.x plugins; this is the legacy-compatible stack, but the v2 line was marked deprecated at 2.19.0 and is not a long-term option. v3: @antv/x6@3.1.8 bundles common, geometry and the official plugins; it requires Node >=20, changes panning, animation and scroller behaviour, and its npm package currently fails native Node ESM and CJS loading (see docs/x6-v2-v3-audit.md). Do not install the deprecated 3.0.0 plugin packages or mix v3 core with 2.x plugins. D3 is the named alternative, but it does not provide X6's editing/plugin layer. Record the actual lockfile, browser baseline and plugin usage before any migration verdict. Choosing v2 is a time-boxed bridge, not a final destination.
